paper.title: Adaptive Bandit Algorithms for Contextual Matching Markets

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual matching markets with stochastic contexts
unmapped: Two-sided matching market: N players matched to K arms each round (N <= K); arms have fixed known strict preferences over players
Each player i has its own unknown parameter theta_i; utility theta_i^T x_j(t); feedback is the noisy reward of every matched pair
Benchmark is the per-round player-optimal stable matching (regret measured per player against its optimal stable share)
Arm contexts drawn i.i.d. each round from a fixed unknown distribution
Difficulty measured by probabilistic minimum preference gap Delta_min (Definition 2)
settings.definition_quote: we consider the setting where the context feature vector $\rx_j(t)$ of each arm $a_j$ is drawn i.i.d. from a fixed but unknown distribution $\gD_{\rx_j}$ at every round $t$. ... $\mU_{i, j}(t) = \theta_i^{\top} \rx_j(t)$ ... $Reg_i(T) = \sum_{t = 1}^T \mU_i^*(t) - \mathbb{E} [\sum_{t = 1}^T y_{i}(t)]$

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual matching markets with adversarial contexts
unmapped: Two-sided matching market with known arm preferences; contexts may be chosen arbitrarily (adaptive adversary)
Regret is the alpha-approximate Delta-optimal stable regret: benchmark is the optimal stable share when delta_min(t) > Delta and alpha times the epsilon-optimal stable share otherwise
Access to an offline (alpha, gamma, eps)-approximation oracle
settings.definition_quote: we now analyze worst-case scenarios in which no assumptions are placed on context generation, i.e., contexts may even be chosen by an adaptive adversary. ... $Reg_i^{\alpha, \Delta}(T) = \sum_{t = 1}^T [\mU_i^*(t) \ind{\delta_{\min}(t) > \Delta} + \alpha \mU^{\varepsilon}_{i}(t) \ind{\delta_{\min}(t) \leq \Delta}] - \mathbb{E} [\sum_{t = 1}^T y_i(t)]$

symbols.Delta_pref: minimum preference gap: sup{Delta : P(delta_min >= Delta) >= 1 - log T/(T Delta^2)} (Definition 2)

tuning: eta = R sqrt(d log((1+T B_x^2/lambda)/delta)) + lambda^{1/2} B_theta

source.label: thm:stochastic_context_upper_bound
source.quote: Assume that the environment follows Assumption~\ref{assume:bound_context}, \ref{assume:bound_noise} and \ref{assume:bound_preference}, and the contexts are stochastic. Following the BARB algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i(T) = \gO (\frac{\log^2 T}{\Delta_{\min}^2} + \frac{\log T}{\Delta_{\min}^2}) = \gO (\frac{\log^2 T}{\Delta_{\min}^2})$.

results.notes: Per-player regret against per-round player-optimal stable matching. Delta_min is the paper's probabilistic gap, not the canonical smallest gap, so declared as Delta_pref. Proof shows explicit bound 64 B_y(eta^2 N d log((T+dλ)/(dλ))/Δ^2 + 3 log T/Δ^2) + B_y(1+N); O hides N, d.

conditions: Assumption 5: CDF of delta_min satisfies F(Delta) <= c Delta for Delta <= Delta_0
Assumptions 1-3 (bounded contexts, subgaussian noise, bounded parameters)

source.label: thm:asymptotic_upper_bound
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assume:cdf_linear}, when $T$ is sufficiently large, the regret of the BARB algorithm satisfies $Reg_i(T) = \tilde{\gO}(T^{2/3})$, $\forall i \in [N]$.

results.notes: Instance-independent within the class satisfying Assumption 5 (constants depend on c). Follows from Delta_min >= (log T/(cT))^{1/3}.

symbols.f_c: constant f(c) depending only on the CDF constant c

conditions: instance satisfies Assumption 5 with CDF F_T(Delta) <= c Delta uniformly over T
bound holds for at least one player (max over players)

source.label: thm:asymptotic_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $N = K = 3$. For any policy $\pi$, there exists an instance satisfying Assumption~\ref{assume:cdf_linear} such that for some constants $c,\Delta_0 > 0$, when $\Delta \leq \Delta_0$, the CDF of $\delta_{\min}$ obeys $F_T(\Delta) \leq c \Delta$ for all $T\ge1$. Then at least one player suffers regret $\Omega(T^{2/3})$, i.e., there exists $i \in [N]$ such that $Reg_i(T) \geq f(c) T^{2/3}$, where $f(c)$ depends only on $c$.

results.notes: Proof via change of measure (two instances differing in one entry; Bretagnolle-Huber) by contradiction; context distribution depends on T (tau = T^{-1/3}). Lower bound is on max over players of per-player regret.

symbols.lam_tilde: lower bound on minimum eigenvalue of the context covariance matrix (Assumption 4)

tuning: initial exploration length T_1, doubled across batches

source.label: thm:betc_upper_bound
source.quote: Assume that the environment follows Assumption~\ref{assume:bound_context}, \ref{assume:bound_noise} and \ref{assume:bound_preference}. Further, assume that the context distribution follows Assumption~\ref{assume:min_eigenvalue}, following the Batched-ETC algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i(T) = \gO (\frac{\log T}{\tilde{\lambda}^2 \Delta_{\min}^2} + \frac{\log T}{\Delta_{\min}^2})$.

results.notes: Explicit bound in proof includes 6NK log2(4 sqrt2 Delta_1/Delta_min) + B_y(1+NK) terms.

symbols.Delta_par: algorithm input Delta defining the regret benchmark threshold

conditions: access to an (alpha, gamma, eps)-approximation oracle (e.g. alpha = 1/floor(log2 N + 2))
tuning: eta = R sqrt(d log((1+T B_x^2/lambda)/delta)) + lambda^{1/2} B_theta, delta = 1/T

source.label: thm:adversarial_context_upper_bound
source.quote: Following the AdECO algorithm with parameter $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$, the $\alpha$-approximate $\Delta$-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i^{\alpha, \Delta}(T) = \gO (\frac{Nd \log^2 T}{(\Delta - \varepsilon)^2} + \frac{\Delta + \varepsilon}{2} \cdot T)$. $\Delta$ is an algorithmic input, and the above regret bound holds uniformly for any choice of $\Delta$.

results.notes: Quantity is the alpha-approximate Delta-optimal stable regret (mixed benchmark depending on Delta), hence 'other'.

source.label: thm:adversarial_context_upper_bound
source.quote: By setting $\Delta = \gO(T^{-1/3})$, $\varepsilon = \Delta / 2$, we have the regret upper bound as $\gO(T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: As stated in the theorem; plugging into the general bound gives N d log^2 T T^{2/3}, so the stated O(T^{2/3}) hides log and N,d factors. Benchmark depends on Delta, which is tuned with T.
